runtimeContract.legalScope: Confirm the actual material/process/jurisdiction. Do not infer hazmat, HAZWOPER, BBP, PSM, laboratory-standard or agricultural-WPS coverage from a catalog label.
runtimeContract.deduplication: One current member/course requirement across overlapping services and roles, preserving source links and separate practical requirements.

courses.title: Hazardous-material transportation: recognition and safe handoff

roleMappings.trigger: Only after the actual material/load classification and the person’s shipping, packaging, marking, loading, unloading or transport function are confirmed. A truck, waste, chemical or fuel-service label alone is insufficient.
roleMappings.rationale: Teach recognition, containment, inconsistent shipment information and safe handoff for the person’s actual regulated transport function. General driving or working near a shipment does not establish that function.

roleMappings.trigger: Only personnel actually preparing/checking hazardous-material shipment information or coordinating a function affecting its transport safety; confirm material, function and transport mode. Ordinary dispatch, passenger booking, payroll and desk brokerage alone do not trigger this rule.
roleMappings.rationale: A shipping clerk or dispatcher can affect hazardous-material safety without driving. Bind the knowledge to that assigned function rather than every office role or everyone employed by a transport company.

roleMappings.trigger: Only the actual driver/loader assigned to a confirmed hazardous-material movement, including waste when classified accordingly; not every driver or apparently chemical load.
roleMappings.rationale: Add the recognition foundation when driving/loading really involves the relevant material. This does not create a hazmat endorsement or replace vehicle/cargo/mode-specific instruction.

courses.title: Hazardous waste and spill response: role limits and safe handoffs

roleMappings.role: Waste handlers, environmental field personnel and operating supervisors
roleMappings.trigger: Confirm actual waste/site conditions and assigned task within a covered hazardous-waste operation or hazardous-substance emergency/cleanup interface. Routine nonhazardous disposal and a waste company label are not sufficient.
roleMappings.rationale: Teach role limits, changing conditions, zones, contamination interfaces and safe handoff at the assessed operation; the foundation does not assign a HAZWOPER response level.

roleMappings.role: Assigned oil-spill responders and response supervisors
roleMappings.trigger: Only an actually assigned hazardous-substance/oil-spill response role, with the relevant response phase, conditions and program applicability confirmed.
roleMappings.rationale: Response recognition and handoff knowledge supports the designated team without granting technician, specialist, incident-command or rescue qualification.

roleMappings.role: Assigned responders, fire-service personnel and response coordinators
roleMappings.trigger: Only confirmed hazardous-substance emergency duties under the actual response plan; ordinary first-aid or unrelated fire-service work is not automatically covered.
roleMappings.rationale: Keep incident recognition and safe boundaries distinct from full responder-level training and practical capability.

roleMappings.trigger: Only the person actually responsible for the confirmed covered waste/response program and its role/phase handoffs.
roleMappings.rationale: Program owners need to recognize what the foundation does not establish and retain employer/method, medical and practical requirements rather than close the entire gap from an online pass.

courses.title: Process safety and operating-procedure competence

roleMappings.role: Assigned process operators, maintenance roles and site management
roleMappings.trigger: Only actual operation, maintenance, process control or assigned process-safety responsibilities after the process/material/safeguard scope is confirmed. Determine applicable PSM regime and exclusions; a plant, refinery or terminal label is not proof of legal coverage.
roleMappings.rationale: Teach process-state, procedure, safeguard, mechanical-integrity, change and handback judgment for actual process duties. Do not assign merely because an engineer works at a desk for a process client.

roleMappings.role: Fuel, gas and process operating or maintenance roles
roleMappings.trigger: Confirm the person’s actual process/containment intervention and operating-procedure responsibility, not merely product sales, transport scheduling or office advice.
roleMappings.rationale: A process worker needs knowledge of the specific loss-of-control pathways and limits of their authority; this course grants no operating, bypass, test or restart permission.

roleMappings.role: Electrical/instrument technicians, commissioning personnel and supervisors
roleMappings.trigger: Only actual work affecting process controls or protective functions, after site/process scope and assigned commissioning/maintenance responsibility are confirmed. IT desk configuration unrelated to safety/process behavior is excluded.
roleMappings.rationale: Teach preservation of process safeguards and controlled change/handback when the actual electrical/instrument task affects the process. Technical electrical and functional-safety competence remain separate.

roleMappings.trigger: Only assigned ownership of the confirmed process-safety/operating-procedure program or its change/readiness decisions, not general membership-admin access.
roleMappings.rationale: Recognize the evidence and responsibilities needed to maintain the process system; foundation completion cannot substitute for actual process information, safe procedures or technical approval.

courses.title: Bloodborne pathogens and occupational exposure controls

roleMappings.role: Licensed clinical personnel and medical interface coordinator
roleMappings.trigger: Only actual clinical/first-aid tasks with reasonably anticipated occupational contact with human blood or OPIM. Desk referral/medical-record coordination alone is excluded.
roleMappings.rationale: Provide exposure-control and prompt confidential-response knowledge to the exposed clinical worker; neither this course nor the service label establishes a clinical licence.

roleMappings.role: Hospitality, housekeeping, laundry and personal-service personnel
roleMappings.trigger: Only confirmed blood/OPIM-contaminated laundry, personal-care or cleanup duties with reasonably anticipated occupational contact; ordinary clean linen, accommodation or housekeeping alone is excluded.
roleMappings.rationale: Support contamination-pathway recognition, sharps/laundry handoff and exposure response for the actual exposed function, not every cleaner or laundry employee.

roleMappings.trigger: Only actual human-remains handling or related contaminated-material duties with reasonably anticipated blood/OPIM contact; funeral office administration and transport booking alone are excluded.
roleMappings.rationale: The funeral service label supports a potential exposed handling function, not a clinical qualification. Bind the foundation to the actual handling duty and keep employer controls and practical training open.

roleMappings.trigger: Only an actual assigned first-aid/response duty in which occupational blood/OPIM contact is reasonably anticipated, as established by the employer exposure determination; witnessing an injury is insufficient.
roleMappings.rationale: Teach the exposure-control and post-exposure interface for the assigned role without treating every employee as a bloodborne-exposed responder.

courses.qualificationBoundary: Written completion does not establish clinical qualification, cleanup or sharps-handling competence, employer-specific exposure-control implementation, interactive Q&A, vaccination or confidential medical follow-up. Those require the appropriate employer, assessor and clinical processes.
courses.remainingRequirements: Knowledge foundation only. Keep actual employer/method instruction, applicable approved training/credentials, medical arrangements, qualified practical evaluation and employer/site authorization separately outstanding.

courses.title: Food hygiene, allergens and catering controls

roleMappings.role: Food handlers, kitchen staff and camp supervisors
roleMappings.trigger: Only actual food receiving, preparation, storage, service, allergen-control or food-supervision duties. Accommodation-only, security, office and ordinary facilities roles are excluded.
roleMappings.rationale: Teach food-chain hygiene, allergen and measured process controls for the person’s real catering function. The FDA model is not automatically local law or a food-handler credential.

roleMappings.trigger: Only actual prepared-food/ingredient transport or receiving handoff with food identity, allergen, temperature or contamination-control responsibility; ordinary camp freight transport is excluded.
roleMappings.rationale: Meal delivery can affect food safety without making the driver a cook. Add food-handoff knowledge while preserving separate transport and practical qualification.

roleMappings.trigger: Only actual canteen food-contact-equipment maintenance and hygiene/contamination handback responsibilities; ordinary workshop repair with no food-chain interface is excluded.
roleMappings.rationale: The source specifically concerns canteen equipment. Teach the food-contact contamination/handover interface, not a claim that the repairer is qualified to cook or supervise catering.

courses.title: Laboratory chemical hygiene and analytical task safety

roleMappings.trigger: Only actual laboratory sample preparation, chemical/reagent use or hazardous analytical work; confirm the method, material and laboratory-use scope. Desk interpretation, sealed-sample courier work and field-only readings are excluded.
roleMappings.rationale: Teach sample identity, chemical hygiene, ventilation, equipment and waste decisions in the actual analytical task. The foundation does not validate a method or establish specialized biological/radiation competence.

roleMappings.trigger: Only confirmed laboratory instrument service with chemical/residual, contaminated-equipment or chemical-hygiene handoff responsibilities. A field instrument technician does not acquire laboratory scope from the title alone.
roleMappings.rationale: Provide chemical-hygiene interface knowledge for instrument service; actual model-specific electrical, pressure, analytical and repair competence stays separately assessed.

roleMappings.role: Research scientists, analysts and research program owner
roleMappings.trigger: Only actual laboratory chemical or sample-method work or assigned chemical-hygiene oversight, not desk R&D, modeling, literature review or grant administration.
roleMappings.rationale: R&D can include laboratories but does not prove bench exposure. Attach the foundation only to confirmed chemical-hygiene duties and retain method-specific requirements.

courses.title: Pesticide handling and application task safety

roleMappings.trigger: Only actual pesticide mixing, loading, application, contaminated application-equipment handling or assigned exposure-control supervision. Confirm product, method, jurisdiction and applicability; nonchemical pest control and mowing alone are excluded.
roleMappings.rationale: Teach label-specific boundaries, exposure controls, bystander/environment protection and handoff for the real pesticide function. Agricultural WPS, structural pest control and other uses have different scopes; this is not approved WPS training or an applicator licence.

roleMappings.role: Grounds workers and assigned mower operators
roleMappings.trigger: Only when this individual is additionally assigned a confirmed pesticide function or relevant application-to-entry exposure-control duty. Grounds work, mowing and working for a landscaper do not independently trigger G15 or WPS.
roleMappings.rationale: Preserve the source’s possible grounds/pesticide interface without turning all grounds staff into pesticide handlers. Actual product/task and agricultural-WPS coverage must be separately resolved.

roleMappings.trigger: Only actual pesticide product/method, bystander, entry or exposure-control planning responsibilities confirmed for this individual; general landscape design or desk advice is excluded.
roleMappings.rationale: A landscape consultant may affect a pesticide plan, but a generic consultancy label does not prove that responsibility. Knowledge of task boundaries is separate from authority to apply or certify compliance.
